name: stacked-gzip-then-zstd
description: Stacked codings are peeled right-to-left: `gzip, zstd` is zstd(gzip(body)) and zstd comes off first.
grounding: RFC 9110 8.4 lists codings in the order they were applied, so the last listed is the outermost. Peeling left-to-right hands gzip's decoder a zstd frame and fails on the very first layer, which is the only reason this asymmetry is testable at all.
notes: `layers` in this corpus is stated in the same order as the header: left is applied first, so a consumer builds the body by applying `layers` left-to-right and decodes by peeling right-to-left.
